Document Standard

UNYRA Premium Document Standard

This standard governs premium internal document design for UNYRA GROUP LLC.

Guidance Standard

Guidance Source / UNYRA-Premium-Document-Standard.md

Guidance TypeDocument StandardOpen Document Standard TopPrimary SurfaceBrand GuidelinesOpen Brand GuidelinesOperating FocusLayout / Typography / Composition ControlOpen Reading
Guidance TrackDocument StandardOpen Guidance StandardsReference SurfaceApproved CompositionsOpen Approved CompositionsGovernance SurfaceVisual StandardOpen Visual Standard

It applies to dashboards, invoices, purchase documents, supplier approvals, intake sheets, and founder-facing rollups.

Standard ControlCurrent Standard
StatusActive premium document standard
PurposeGovern UNYRA's premium internal and founder-facing document design so operating records, dashboards, previews, and future PDF exports feel controlled, executive-ready, and institution-grade.
Source ruleUse the approved visual identity, approved compositions, exported visual standard, branded preview area, and institutional communication style guide before changing document hierarchy, layout, or outward-facing presentation.
Decision ruleFavor restrained structure, fast founder comprehension, source-record clarity, and approved brand usage over decorative redesign.
Asset protectionDo not redraw, stretch, recolor, restyle, or replace approved brand assets or protected template masters while applying this document standard.

1. Visual IntentLink

Every document should communicate operational control, not decoration.

Desired signalRequired expression
PremiumThe layout feels deliberate, spacious, and finished.
RestrainedVisual emphasis is selective rather than loud.
CorporateThe document reads as suitable for executive, procurement, finance, and compliance review.
Internationally credibleThe structure feels appropriate for cross-border trade and institutional counterparties.
Fast to scanThe important answer can be understood in under 30 seconds.

2. Brand Source of TruthLink

Use the following approved brand assets first.

Asset sourceRequired use
00_brand/01_assets/05_approved-compositions/Use horizontal logo lockups and circular seal versions before creating any new composition.
00_brand/01_assets/04_signatures/Use approved signature layouts for founder, business-development, or outbound signature treatment.
Approved compositionsDo not redraw, stretch, recolor, or restyle approved compositions without explicit approval.

3. Color RolesLink

Color roleValueUse
Primary navy#08121EHeaders, titles, structure, and authority.
Support navy#102436Secondary framing and deep UI surfaces.
Gold accent#C2A071Accents, highlights, section rules, and positive emphasis.
Strong gold accent#9D7646Darker accent text or restrained premium emphasis.
Ivory#F7F3ECSoft premium backgrounds and document warmth.
Canvas#F3EEE6Background canvas and quiet surface contrast.
Muted text#5B6672Secondary information and supporting metadata.
Muted dark#2A3742Body copy, table detail, and secondary authority.

Gold should be present, but restrained.

4. Typography RulesLink

Typography ruleRequired behavior
Data and operationsUse a crisp sans serif for data, tables, and operational content.
Document headersUse larger, more spacious title styling for document headers and founder summaries.
HeadingsKeep headings bold and short.
Micro-labelsUse uppercase micro-labels for metadata and section identifiers.
Density controlAvoid dense paragraphs when a list, table, or grid communicates faster.

5. Layout RulesLink

Layout ruleRequired behavior
MarginsUse generous page margins.
MastheadKeep the brand masthead compact.
MetadataGroup related metadata into clean cards or aligned detail rows.
Focal areaUse no more than one dominant focal area per page section.
TablesLet tables breathe with clear row spacing and subtle dividers.
Section architecturePrefer two or three strong sections over many small fragmented boxes.

6. Dashboard RulesLink

Dashboard ruleRequired behavior
Founder answer firstShow the founder what matters first.
Decision hierarchyPut priorities, KPIs, risks, next actions, and blockers before detailed logs.
Table disciplineUse concise tables with only the fields required for a decision.
Risk emphasisHighlight risk or urgency with structure and contrast, not loud warning colors.

7. Document Component SetLink

Preferred reusable components are listed below.

ComponentUse
Premium mastheadEstablish brand authority without overpowering the document.
Metadata gridShow owner, date, status, source, route, and control context.
KPI cardsSurface the few measures that change the decision.
Summary stripGive the founder the fast reading before details.
Clean operational tableOrganize source facts, gates, actions, and records.
Note panelContain important context without breaking the main flow.
Decision cardIsolate approval, blocker, exception, or founder-call requirements.
Approval or signature blockClose the document with accountable authority.

Reuse the shared visual system in 00_brand/03_exports/01_visual-standard/.

8. Print and Export ReadinessLink

Export ruleRequired behavior
Screen and PDF qualityPreviews should render well on screen and remain clean when printed to PDF.
Text protectionAvoid oversized background art behind critical text.
Closing placementKeep signatures, totals, and approval blocks close to the end of each document.
Grayscale resilienceMaintain clear page hierarchy even in grayscale printouts.

9. Approved Preview AreaLink

Preview files live in 00_brand/03_exports/02_preview-docs/.

Preview useStandard
Founder reviewUse previews to evaluate visual quality before template or PDF upgrades.
Visual approvalUse previews as benchmark surfaces for the approved look and hierarchy.
Future PDF conversionKeep previews clean enough to support later export workflows.
Future template upgradesUse previews as design references, not as live operating source records.

They are not source records for live operations.

10. External Communication StandardLink

Customer- and supplier-facing documents should feel like they came from a serious institution.

External standardRequired expression
Header controlUse strong header control and clear brand placement.
Reference clarityInclude explicit subject and reference numbers.
Recipient clarityUse clean recipient blocks.
Attachment disciplineUse disciplined attachment naming.
Action clarityState clear action requests and deadlines.
Signature treatmentUse clean approved signature treatment.
Tone disciplineAvoid casual email styling.
Packet controlIf multiple files are sent together, use a formal transmittal and packet index so the release feels controlled instead of improvised.

The language should also follow 00_brand/02_guidelines/UNYRA-Institutional-Communication-Style-Guide.md so the visual quality and wording quality stay aligned.
